title: test: concurrent C_Initialize/C_Finalize vs. in-flight operations
description:
C_Finalize while another thread is mid-operation is the most dangerous race in any PKCS#11 library. wolfP11 uses g_initialized + g_lock for sequencing but this has not been tested.

Write tests in test/wp11_test_pkcs11_threads.c:

Test 1 — C_Finalize races C_Sign:
- Thread A: tight loop C_SignInit → C_Sign (1000 iterations)
- Thread B: after a random delay (1-10ms), calls C_Finalize
- Success criterion: C_Finalize returns CKR_OK; Thread A gets either CKR_OK or CKR_CRYPTOKI_NOT_INITIALIZED — never a crash or memory corruption
- Run with AddressSanitizer to catch use-after-free in freed session/key structs

Test 2 — double C_Initialize from two threads:
- Thread A and Thread B both call C_Initialize simultaneously
- Success criterion: exactly one returns CKR_OK, the other returns CKR_CRYPTOKI_ALREADY_INITIALIZED — no crash, no double-init of wolfCrypt RNG

Test 3 — C_Finalize races C_OpenSession:
- Thread A: tight loop C_OpenSession → C_CloseSession
- Thread B: calls C_Finalize mid-loop
- Success criterion: no session handles left dangling, no crash

Test 4 — piv_inject_login_impl race (wolfP11-v49):
- Thread A: calls C_Finalize
- Thread B: calls wp11_test_inject_piv_login concurrently
- Success criterion: no TOCTOU crash
- This specifically validates the fix for wolfP11-v49

Compile with -fsanitize=thread,address for all thread tests.
